title: How Marc Lou values and sells a micro startup (3x annualized revenue)
summary: Marc explains a simple valuation formula for micro startups (annualized revenue x 3), when to sell, and how the acquisition process works. He draws on selling GameWidget and Habits Garden, and shares tips to close faster, including building in public to attract buyers.

principles.text: Value a micro startup at roughly annualized revenue x 3; don't overcomplicate valuation.
Don't over-optimize valuation; a few percent isn't worth the hustle versus building more apps.
principles.quote: You can dive deeper into startup valuation. I don’t. It gets overwhelming and gaining 5% here or there isn’t worth the hustle. I’d rather build more apps.

principles.text: Decide to sell using three questions: 10x potential, care about the market, need for money.
principles.quote: Can I 10x the revenue in a year?

principles.text: Small side projects have real value; $1,000 MRR buys years of full-time building runway.
principles.quote: Imagine you grow a weekend project to $1,000 MRR… You have a 2-year pass to quit your job, move to Bali, and build apps full-time.

principles.text: Build in public so buyers trust you; it can lead to direct sales and save listing fees.
principles.quote: It all comes down to trust so build your startups in public: you don’t know it yet but potential buyers are following you and can wire the money to your bank account without asking much

principles.text: Move buyers quickly: drop overly skeptical ones and set deadlines for answers.
principles.quote: Don’t be afraid to follow up and tell buyers you need an answer within 3 days.
